digest.component_or_area: completion verifier budget and criterion validation
propositions: The verifier's step budget exhausts prematurely on legitimate validation, causing valid criteria to fail as unmet when only unproven-within-budget; legitimate use cases (6-14 AC epics) repeatedly trigger false exhaustion at current defaults.

Budget sizing must account for epic child-ticket traversal cost (show_ticket + comments + repo reads = 5-10 requests per child); the formula needs an evidence-surface term: budget = per_criterion × c + child_traversal × direct_children + fixed_overhead.

Re-verification of the same criteria across runs re-proves all evidence from scratch (~10 min per cycle); a cross-run PASS-verdict cache keyed by criterion text and scoped content fingerprint (git blob SHAs of file_impact paths) can credit validated verdicts without re-verification, seeded into the run-scoped CriterionBank with a seeded flag to exclude them from the primary's work surface.

The defaults must be raised (24 steps/criterion, 160 floor-min, 960 clamp-max) and the formula updated to include child-traversal and fixed-overhead terms so 6-AC epics size to ≥80 requests and 15-AC epics to ≥180.

Cached PASS verdicts persist only after validation, invalidate on criterion-text or fingerprint change (including file_impact content changes via blob SHA rotation), and are not invalidated by unrelated commits outside file_impact; ref-scoped verification (--ref <sha> workflows) bind fingerprints to the verified-at ref's tree state to prevent cache-key mismatches.

Seeded verdicts bypass finalizer judgment (echo or omission cannot downgrade a cached PASS record), while same-run finalizer downgrades are preserved to maintain runaway detection; runaway guards (tool_calls_limit, loop detection) remain authoritative and unchanged, with the step budget serving only as a runaway ceiling, not an artificial validation cap.
